sources.text: NPCI/UPI/OC No. 169/2023-24 31st August 2023 To All Member-Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Dear Madam/Sir, **Subject: Enhancement in UPI LITE transaction limit to ₹500** UPI LITE has been designed to play a vital role in reducing infrastructure load on the Core Banking System of the banks. This feature has been making the small value transactions faster and highly reliable for transaction value below ₹200. As per the latest circular issued by RBI on 24th August, 2023 vide Circular No: RBI/2023-24/57 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S526/02-14-003/2023-24 with subject ‘Enhancing transaction limits for Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode’, the upper limit of an offline payment transaction is now increased from ₹200 to ₹500. In view of the above, the per transaction value limit for UPI LITE (Purpose code 44 - Online and 45 - Offline) has now been enhanced to ₹500. The details are as below: | UPI LITE Limit | Previous Limit | New Limit | |---|---|---| | Per Transaction | ₹200 | ₹500 | | Max balance in UPI lite account | ₹2000 | ₹2000 (No change) | The existing UPI pricing shall be applicable for transaction amount ₹201-₹500 for both P2P and P2M transactions. With reference to the above, Member Banks (Payee PSP), Third Party App providers (TPAPs), Merchants and other payment providers are requested to take note of the above enhancement

sources.text: NPCI /UPI/OC No.138/2021-22 March 16, 2022 To, All UPI Member Banks Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Introduction of “On-Device wallet” – UPI Lite for Small Value Transactions UPI has become one of the most preferred digital payment mode for Indian citizens because of ease and convenience, superior user experience, security and interoperability. To realize the vision of billion-a-day payments within the next 3 to 5 years, NPCI has been aggressively innovating and adding new features in UPI from time to time to expand its usage. Various studies on payment systems have observed that about 75% of the total volume of retail transactions (including cash) in India are below ₹100 transaction value. Further, 50% of the total UPI transactions are having a transaction value of up to ₹200/-. To process billion-a-day transactions, entire UPI ecosystem will have to invest heavily in infrastructure upgrade. Large banks have already implemented upgrades, such as separate financial and meta transactions infrastructure, separate endpoints for payment service provider (PSP) / issuer and to provide better technical up time for UPI services, and such banks are getting ready to process three times of current volumes. As an efficient strategy to process large-scale small value digital payments and based on the guidelines issued by RBI for enabling mobile devices to support offline payments vide its circular no. request.query: What is UPI Lite? Explain its purpose in simple terms.

claims.text: UPI Lite is an 'On-Device wallet' functionality designed for small value transactions that allows users to process payments in near offline or complete offline modes.

Its purpose is to reduce the load on core banking systems by enabling faster, highly reliable payments for transaction values below a specific limit without requiring real-time online verification for every debit.
Users can allocate funds from their bank account to the UPI Lite balance stored on their device, which resides in an escrow or designated account at the bank.

In phase 1, UPI Lite will process transactions in near offline mode i.e. debit offline and credit online, and at a later point, UPI Lite will process transactions in complete offline mode i.e. debit and credit both offline. A User of UPI App will have the option to enable UPI Lite i.e. “On-Device wallet” on her/his UPI App. Once enabled, the User can allocate funds from her/his bank account to UPI Lite. Such funds shall reside with the User’s bank in an escrow / pool / designated account and such balance shall reside on-device on the common library (CL) of the User’s UPI App. At present, only debit from UPI Lite balance shall be permitted and all credits to UPI Lite (including refunds, etc.) will be processed online in the User’s bank account maintained in the bank’s core banking system. claims.text: OC 186A states that UPI Tap & Pay through Near Field Communication (NFC) on QR was previously introduced as an additional mode for initiating UPI transactions and is now extended to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals.
Under OC 186A, Users can make contactless (NFC-based) UPI payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on the PoS terminal.

OC 186A requires Members and UPI Application Providers to refer to applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Documents, Technical Specifications, and other instructions issued by NPCI for detailed functional, technical, and operational requirements.
OC 186A mandates that settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for UPI Tap & Pay transactions be carried out in accordance with extant UPI guidelines.
OC 186A directs Members to follow RBI guidelines on Harmonization of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions using authorized Payment Systems.
